A compromised Lambda function with excessive permissions could access Secrets Manager and retrieve credentials for all cloud providers, leading to unauthorized access across multip

Sensitive Cost Data Exposure via S3 [Information Disclosure, Tampering, CWE-200] on S3-RawCostData, S3-ProcessedData, Lambda-CostProcessor: Misconfigured S3 bucket policies or inadequate access controls could allow unauthorized access to sensitive cost data stored in the buckets. An attacker could exploit overly permissive bucket policies to access or modify cost data, potentially leading to data leakage or manipulation of cost reports.

API Gateway Authentication Bypass [Spoofing, Elevation of Privilege, CWE-287] on APIGateway, IAM-Authentication, Lambda-CostAnalyzer: Insufficient API Gateway authentication configuration or vulnerabilities in the authentication mechanism could allow unauthorized access to the API endpoints. An attacker could forge or manipulate authentication tokens to gain unauthorized access to cost management APIs.

DynamoDB Data Manipulation [Tampering, Information Disclosure, Repudiation, CWE-922] on DynamoDB-CostDatabase, Lambda-CostProcessor, Lambda-CostAnalyzer: Overly permissive IAM policies or compromised Lambda functions could allow unauthorized modification of cost data in DynamoDB. An attacker with access to a compromised Lambda function could modify cost data to hide resource usage or manipulate billing information.

EventBridge Rule Manipulation [Tampering, Denial of Service, CWE-284] on EventBridge-Scheduler, Lambda-CostCollector, Lambda-CostProcessor: Attackers with IAM permissions could modify EventBridge rules to disrupt cost data collection timing or frequency. An attacker could modify scheduling rules to prevent cost data collection or overwhelm the system with too frequent collections.
